title: HTTPAPIBody
description: Bounded JSON bodies of the same-origin browser HTTP API. See http-api.md for routes, headers and cookie rules.

secret.description: 256-bit random value encoded as unpadded base64url (43 characters).

verificationCode.description: Short human comparison code. It never authorizes access by itself.

pairPollResponse.title: HTTPPairPollResponse
pairPollResponse.description: An approved response is the only one that sets the session cookie.

namedOption.title: HTTPNamedOption
namedOption.description: A saved project or shell profile, selected by ID. Paths and executables are never sent to the browser.

hostBuild.description: The Termivoa build this computer runs, as version+commit (for example 0.1.0-beta.2+1a2b3c4d5e6f). A peer sends it, so it is untrusted text: ASCII letters, digits and . _ + - only, shown as plain text.

providers.description: Terminal workspace providers found on this computer (for example herdr). Absent or empty when none is installed; the app shows a provider tab only for a computer that lists one.

providerState.title: HTTPProviderState
providerState.description: ready: the host reads the provider. notRunning: installed, but its server does not answer. unsupported: the installed version is too old or its data cannot be read. off: turned off in Settings → Integrations on this computer.

providerItemState.description: Provider state of a terminal, item or group, mapped by the host (docs/herdr-provider.md, State mapping). Known words: blocked, done, working, idle, unknown, none (no agent there). Roll-up order, most urgent first: blocked, done, working, idle, unknown, none. A word, not an enum, so a later provider can add one: the app shows any other word as unknown.

providerId.description: A terminal workspace provider on this computer, for example herdr. See docs/herdr-provider.md.

providerTargetId.description: Opaque handle of one provider terminal, issued by the host in its latest snapshot. For herdr it is <pane ID>.<terminal ID> (for example w2:p4.term_65d0031602b777), so a handle from before a herdr restart never names a new terminal. The host accepts only a handle that is in its latest snapshot.

providerAgentKind.description: An agent kind the provider knows, for example claude. Display text and the agent picker value.

providerHandle.description: Opaque group or item handle from the host's last snapshot. Never a path.

providerInfo.title: HTTPProviderInfo
providerInfo.description: One provider on this computer. enabled and notify are this computer's Integrations settings (all devices). canCreate is true when the provider can make a worktree and start an agent (milestone M2). agentKinds lists the kinds offered by the new-worktree sheet: kinds that herdr itself can start (its agent start kinds) and that already run in this herdr, most used first.

providerTarget.title: HTTPProviderTarget
providerTarget.description: One terminal the phone can open: each agent, plus one terminal for each tab without an agent. label is the tab label. canOpen is false when this provider version cannot attach to it. Terminal titles are never sent (a program sets them, often to the task text).

providerItem.title: HTTPProviderItem
providerItem.description: One row under a group (for herdr, one workspace: the main checkout or a linked worktree). openTarget is the terminal a tap opens (the most urgent agent, else the active tab's terminal); it is absent when nothing can be opened. stateSince is when the host first saw the current state.

providerGroup.title: HTTPProviderGroup
providerGroup.description: One project row (for herdr, a git repository and its worktrees, or a workspace outside git). state is the roll-up of its items.

providerSnapshotResponse.title: HTTPProviderSnapshotResponse
providerSnapshotResponse.description: GET /api/v1/providers/{provider}: the host's cached view, never older than about 5 s while state is ready. groups is empty unless state is ready. truncated is true when the host cut the list at its item limits or at its 256 KiB body budget.

providerOpenRequest.title: HTTPProviderOpenRequest
providerOpenRequest.description: POST /api/v1/providers/{provider}/open. The host opens (or reuses) one in-memory provider session attached to that terminal. columns and rows are the phone's fitted grid: a new attach starts at that size, which herdr gives the pane on the computer until the session ends. A reused session keeps its size.

providerSession.title: HTTPProviderSession
providerSession.description: A provider session: a broker terminal session that runs the provider's attach client. It lives in broker memory only (never in the sessions table, never in GET /api/v1/sessions) and is attached over /api/v1/ws like any session. It has no project or shell profile, so rename, terminate, uploads, tasks, preview and worktrees do not apply to it.

providerOpenResponse.title: HTTPProviderOpenResponse
providerOpenResponse.description: The session to show in Live. reused is true when the host already had a live session for this terminal.

providerUpdateRequest.title: HTTPProviderUpdateRequest
providerUpdateRequest.description: PATCH /api/v1/providers/{provider}: Settings → Integrations on this computer.

providerCreateRequest.title: HTTPProviderCreateRequest
providerCreateRequest.description: POST /api/v1/providers/{provider}/create (milestone M2): a new worktree in a group, and optionally an agent in it with a first prompt. name is the new branch and worktree name; the host also refuses a name that ends in .lock or has more than 4 parts. agent must be one of the provider's agentKinds. prompt must hold no control characters other than tab and line feed (no ESC, no other C0 or C1, no DEL).

providerCreateResponse.title: HTTPProviderCreateResponse
providerCreateResponse.description: The new item and the terminal to open. The worktree exists whenever this is returned. agentStarted is false when no agent was asked for or the agent did not start; problem then says why (agentNotReady: it started but waits at a question; agentFailed: it did not start; promptFailed: it started, the first prompt was not sent).

protocolRevision.description: Additive revision of protocol v1 (protocol/v1/revision.json). On the settings response, protocolRevision is this computer's revision and minProtocolRevision the oldest app revision it still serves. See http-api.md, Protocol revision.

computerOrigin.description: Canonical origin of a Termivoa computer: https, lowercase DNS host of at least two labels, default port (no explicit port), no trailing dot, path, user or query.

computerLabel.description: Display name of a computer on this phone, by default the first DNS label of its origin. Never identity.

computerState.title: HTTPComputerState
computerState.description: pending: recorded before pairing with the peer so the app's CSP allows it; short expiry, shown nowhere. confirmed: the app read the peer's settings with the peer's own cookie.

tailnetNode.title: TailnetNode
tailnetNode.description: A Tailscale node from the computer's own tailscale status. id is the stable node ID. owner is the login name of a user-owned node and is absent for tagged nodes, which carry tags instead. Display and pinning data, never authentication.

computer.title: HTTPComputer
computer.description: A confirmed peer computer in the calling device's own list on this (home) computer.

computerListResponse.title: HTTPComputerListResponse
computerListResponse.description: GET /api/v1/computers: the calling device's confirmed computers. Pending entries are never listed.

computerAddRequest.title: HTTPComputerAddRequest
computerAddRequest.description: POST /api/v1/computers. state pending records or refreshes a short-lived pending entry before pairing; confirmed confirms an existing entry (or renames a confirmed one) after the peer's settings were read.

computerAddResponse.title: HTTPComputerAddResponse
computerAddResponse.description: The saved entry and the peer's node as seen in this computer's own tailscale status, for the app's confirm sheet.

computerOfferRequest.title: HTTPComputerOfferRequest
computerOfferRequest.description: POST /api/v1/computers/offer, sent by a new computer's broker to the home computer the user named (pterm pair --via). origin is the new computer's own canonical origin; grant is a single-use grant made on the new computer and bound to home's origin and pinned node. No authentication; the gateway refuses any Origin or Sec-Fetch-* header and answers 204 for every well-formed offer. See http-api.md, Found on your network.

foundComputer.title: HTTPFoundComputer
foundComputer.description: One computer that waits to be added. origin and grant come from its offer; label is the first DNS label of its host from home's own tailscale status, never from the offer. expiresAt is when home drops the offer.

computerFoundResponse.title: HTTPComputerFoundResponse
computerFoundResponse.description: GET /api/v1/computers/found: unexpired offers of computers in home's own tailnet (same owner, untagged) that are not yet confirmed for the calling device, sorted by origin, one per origin.

pushPublicKey.description: Uncompressed P-256 public key (65 bytes) as unpadded base64url.

pushEndpoint.description: Push service URL from PushSubscription.endpoint. The broker accepts only https URLs on a known push service host.

pushConfigResponse.title: HTTPPushConfigResponse
pushConfigResponse.description: The broker's VAPID application server public key.

auth.$comment: 16-byte push authentication secret as unpadded base64url.

previewConfigResponse.title: HTTPPreviewConfigResponse
previewConfigResponse.description: GET /api/v1/preview. origin is the separate preview origin that the phone app may frame (for example https://host:8443); it is absent when the gateway serves no previews.

pushTestResponse.title: HTTPPushTestResponse
pushTestResponse.description: How many of the calling device's subscriptions accepted the test notification.

uploadContentType.title: HTTPUploadContentType
uploadContentType.description: Image type detected by the broker from the file's magic bytes. The client never names it.

uploadRequest.title: HTTPUploadRequest
uploadRequest.description: One image for the session's project folder. data is the file, standard padded base64, 1 byte to 5 MiB decoded. The client name is never sent: the broker names the file.

uploadResponse.title: HTTPUploadResponse
uploadResponse.description: Where the broker saved the image, relative to the session's project folder.
